title: Black-body radiation; Compton scattering; Mass defect and binding energy; Fission and reactors; Fusion; Decay law and half-life
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; T04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; T04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; T04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N03-1#N.2, N04-1#N.3a, N05-1#N.2a, N06-1#N.4b, Q05-1#N.3b, T04-1#N.3, N03-1#N.5b, N04-1#N.12, Q05-1#N.6b, T04-1#N.8, N03-1#N.12b, Q05-1#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Photon
items.clue: Particle of light with energy hc/λ and momentum h/λ that always travels at c.

items.label: Black body
items.clue: Ideal object that absorbs perfectly and emits as well as is possible at its temperature.

items.label: Peak wavelength
items.clue: Position of the top of the spectrum curve: about 500 nm for the Sun, 850 nm for a red star.

items.label: Stefan–Boltzmann law
items.clue: States that total power radiated is proportional to surface area times T to the fourth power.

questions.stem: Predict first. Radioactive decay is described as random and spontaneous. Which statement correctly describes what this means?

options.text: A nucleus decays when a collision or a rise in temperature gives it the energy it needs.
Nuclei decay roughly in the order in which they formed, but their ages cannot be known.
The count rate varies so unpredictably that the half-life of a sample cannot be measured.
When a given nucleus decays cannot be predicted, and outside conditions do not alter its chance.

questions.stem: A nucleus of mass M, initially at rest, splits into two fragments of masses m₁ and m₂ and no other particles. Which expression gives the total kinetic energy of the two fragments just after the split?

options.text: (M − m₁ − m₂)c
(M − m₁ − m₂)/c²
(M − m₁ − m₂)c²
(m₁ + m₂)c² − Mc²

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of nuclear fission?

options.text: Plutonium-239, after taking in a neutron, breaks up into two medium-mass nuclei.
Two hydrogen-2 nuclei join to form a helium-3 nucleus, releasing a neutron and energy.
A uranium-238 nucleus absorbs a neutron and becomes a heavier uranium-239 nucleus.
A water molecule splits apart into two separate hydrogen atoms and a single oxygen atom.

questions.stem: Which statement about the total mass of the particles taking part in fission, fusion and radioactive decay is correct?

options.text: Fission and fusion change the total mass, but radioactive decay leaves the total mass unchanged.
None of the three processes change the total mass, since mass is conserved as in chemical reactions.
Each of the three processes lowers the total mass by converting some of the nucleons into energy.
In each of the three processes the total mass changes, while the total nucleon number stays the same.

questions.stem: Predict first. An X-ray photon collides with a free electron that is initially at rest, and a photon emerges moving in a new direction. How does the emerging photon compare with the incident photon?

options.text: Its wavelength is shorter, since it has given energy to the electron
Its wavelength is longer, since it has given up energy to the electron
Its wavelength is unchanged, since it simply bounces off the electron
Its speed is now less than c, since it has given energy to the electron

questions.stem: Predict first. A black body is heated to a higher temperature. How does its emission spectrum change?

options.text: It emits more at every wavelength, and the peak moves to a longer wavelength.
It emits more at every wavelength, and its peak moves to a shorter wavelength.
Its peak moves to shorter wavelengths, so it emits less at long wavelengths.
It emits only one wavelength, λ_max, which gets shorter as it gets hotter.

questions.stem: A sample of iodine-131 has a half-life of 8.0 days. A second sample contains twice as many iodine-131 nuclei. What is the half-life of the second sample?

options.text: 16 days, since twice as many nuclei have to decay before half are gone
8.0 days, since each nucleus has the same chance of decaying in a given time
4.0 days, since twice as many nuclei give twice as many decays per second
It cannot be predicted, since the decay of each individual nucleus is a random event

questions.stem: The bar chart shows the total binding energy of each of two nuclei, X and Y, and the total binding energy of the fragments that each nucleus would form by fission. Which claim is supported by the chart?

options.text: Fission of X would need an energy input, since X's fragments have a greater total binding energy than X.
Neither fission would need an energy input, since splitting a nucleus releases energy.
Both fissions would need an energy input, since energy is needed to break a nucleus apart.
Fission of Y would need an energy input, since Y's fragments have less total binding energy than Y.

questions.stem: An X-ray photon of wavelength 5.00 × 10⁻¹¹ m is scattered by a free electron that is initially at rest, and the scattered photon moves at 37° to the incident direction. What is the wavelength of the scattered photon? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s.
A small metal sphere of radius 5.0 cm is heated to 527 °C. Treat it as a black body and take σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. What power does the sphere emit as thermal radiation?
A sample contains 8.0 g of a radioactive isotope whose half-life is 5.3 years. What mass of the isotope has decayed after 12 years?

A photon with energy E, moving in the +x-direction, collides with a free electron that is initially at rest. After the collision, the scattered photon moves in the +y-direction with energy E′. The speed of light is c. Which expression gives the magnitude of the electron's momentum just after the collision?

options.text: √(E²+E′²)/c
E/c
